sequence_strategy: Email 1 answers Mr. Castillo's request in his own terms (three 24/7 Atacama lithium sites, costly and hazardous contracted crews, Anglo American referral, Q3 budget conversation) and uses SQM's own FlytBase and Adentu deployment as the single proof point, then asks about Metrics and the Economic Buyer and offers two Santiago-time slots. If he goes quiet, each follow-up adds one new useful item aimed at a different gap: Email 2 gives the IT and connectivity precedent and turns the call into a Decision Criteria session, Email 3 gives the referrer's own peer deployment plus a forwardable summary so he can carry the case internally (Champion, Decision Process), and Email 4 closes the loop, offers to hold until the Q3 budget conversation and asks about the vendor onboarding path (Paper Process). The asks get smaller as the sequence goes on, and every email stands on its own in the same thread.

tone_adaptation.seniority: He is Head of Operations for a division, so the tone is formal, brief and peer-level ('Dear Mr. Castillo', no first name, no pressure). It leads with outcomes and crew safety and keeps specifications out of the body.
tone_adaptation.industry: Mining and lithium extraction: the content is about crew safety, scheduled coverage of remote sites, uptime and a cost case. Acronyms are spelled out and there are no drone specs. Proof comes from mining deployments only: SQM's own 678 km² operation in northern Chile (S1) and Anglo American's Quellaveco mine (S32).
tone_adaptation.stated_context: Each email mirrors what he told us: three large 24/7 sites in the Atacama, contracted crews that are expensive and hazardous, the Anglo American referral (named in Email 1 and used as the peer case in Email 3) and the Q3 budget conversation (the pilot scope and cost case are framed for it, and Email 4 offers to hold until then). He is in Chile, so times are in America/Santiago and Email 1 offers to continue in Spanish.

emails.send_when: Same business hour as the inbound (Thursday 5 November 2026, Santiago business hours), in reply to his original thread
emails.goal: Confirm we understood his request, show SQM's own verified precedent and book a 30-minute discovery call
emails.subject: Re: Autonomous inspection for our Atacama lithium sites
emails.body:
Dear Mr. Castillo,

Thank you for your note and the Anglo American referral. You need drone-based inspection for three large 24/7 lithium extraction sites in the Atacama, because contracted crews are expensive and hazardous, ahead of a Q3 budget conversation.

The aim: fewer people on hazardous rounds, more frequent scheduled coverage, and a cost case ready for Q3.

Your company already has a reference point: SQM's digital innovation team runs docked drones with Adentu and FlytBase across a 678 km² operation in northern Chile, and the published case study reports inspection time cut from days to hours with more than 95 percent mission reliability.

A pilot could start with one dock at one site.

Two questions to prepare:
1. Which three sites do you have in mind, and how often do crews inspect them today?
2. Who else will take part in the Q3 budget conversation?

Would a 30-minute call on Tuesday 10 November at 10:00 or Wednesday 11 November at 15:00 (Santiago time) suit you? You are welcome to bring a safety or IT colleague.

Con gusto podemos continuar en español.

Kind regards,
Samruddhi Sontakke
Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: He asked us directly and is a P1 lead (ICP fit 91), so the reply must go out within the hour. Mirroring his own words earns agreement, and SQM's own deployment (S1) is the most relevant proof that exists: same company, same desert, same type of inspection. The two questions cover the biggest scoping and budget gaps without turning the reply into a form.
emails.why_next: If he does not reply, Email 2 answers a likely IT and connectivity concern with a new fact from the same deployment and turns the call into a Decision Criteria session, a different gap from Email 1.
emails.success_signal: He accepts one of the two slots or names the three sites and the people in the Q3 budget conversation.

emails.send_when: +2 business days, Tuesday 10 November 2026 around 12:00 Santiago time (after the first proposed slot passes), same thread
emails.goal: Add the IT and connectivity precedent and restate the call with a new time, framed around his success criteria

Dear Mr. Castillo,

Since Anglo American referred you, their case may help: at Quellaveco in Peru they run a FlytBase drone-in-a-box with regional partner UAV Latam, flying scheduled inspections without on-site pilots.

A summary you can forward internally:

Business Development, FlytBase
emails.why_this_email_now: After two touches without a reply, the likely blocker is that he needs to bring colleagues in. A peer deployment from the company that referred him, plus a five-line summary, gives him something to forward and coaches him as a champion. The ask shrinks to a yes/no.
emails.why_next: If he is still silent, Email 4 closes the loop politely, ties the next contact to his own Q3 timeline and asks about the vendor onboarding path.
emails.success_signal: He forwards the summary, copies a colleague, or says yes to a call.

emails.why_this_email_now: Three touches without a reply means it is time to stop. A respectful close tied to his own Q3 timeline keeps the relationship warm and avoids guilt. emails.success_signal: He names a date to reconnect or refers us to a procurement or supply chain contact.
